title: Price-book segmentation and commitment credit routing playbook
creator: Priya Patel
description: Create an operational playbook and routing ruleset for handling non-bug customer requests related to pricing/packaging, committed credits, and marketplace offsets. This ticket scopes the price-book segmentation logic (how we classify requests by type and dollar impact), automated routing decisions for billing ops vs sales/finance, and deterministic credit allocation rules when customers have both commitments and marketplace credits. The goal is to reduce manual triage time, ensure consistent customer outcomes, and provide a clear audit trail for downstream invoicing and cost allocation. Deliverables: documented playbook, intake form fields, routing matrix, sample SQLs for impact estimation, and a handoff checklist for Billing Ops.
acceptance_criteria: A central playbook document exists describing segmentation tiers, routing decisions, and fallback behavior
An intake form prototype (Console + intake sheet template) with mandatory fields to compute estimated financial impact
Routing matrix that maps request surface (commitment change, invoice adjustment, marketplace offset, refund/credit) to owning team and SLA
Automated rules defined for credit precedence (commitment vs marketplace) with three example scenarios and calculations
Billing Ops runbook and audit checklist that reduces time-to-resolution by >= 30% in pilot
comments: 2026-02-20 Priya P: Kickoff — captured scope with Finance and Billing Ops. Agreed to prototype intake form and prioritize automation of credit routing logic.
2026-02-26 Ethan M: Initial segmentation draft posted. Proposed three tiers: low-touch (< $5k), medium ($5k–$50k), high (> $50k) and emergency SLA lane. Need finance validation on thresholds.
2026-03-01 Finance (Samir R): Confirmed thresholds are reasonable; suggested splitting medium into recurring vs one-off commitments for accounting treatment.
2026-03-04 Billing Ops (Logan C): Provided examples of past tickets where manual credit allocation caused double-counting — will share anonymized spreadsheets.

2026-03-09 Design (Aisha K): Intake wireframes complete; added mandatory fields to capture Marketplace ID, Commitment Contract ID, invoice number, and requested outcome (offset, invoice reissue, credit memo).
notes: Routing rules (draft): if request_type == 'commitment-change' -> route to Sales Ops; if request_type == 'invoice-adjust' AND marketplace_credit_present -> route to Billing Ops with 'credit-eval' flag; emergency SLA lane for contract disputes over $100k.

Credit precedence (proposed): 1) Apply committed credits up to committed usage; 2) Apply marketplace promotional credits for overage or special discounts only when explicitly marked by Finance; 3) Never apply marketplace offsets retroactively to committed-period invoices without CFO sign-off.
Edge-case: customers with cross-account marketplace credits require manual accounting mapping. Mark as 'requires-finance' in the intake form.
Operational checklist: verify contract ID, compute delta impact, run sample ledger SQL (example query link in Confluence), attach invoice PDF, and create billing memo template to send to customer.

Open questions: Should we expose a simplified estimate to customers in the Console when they open the request? (Pro: reduces clarifying back-and-forth. Con: risk of displaying incorrect estimates before finance review.)
resolution_notes: Pending: execute 2-week pilot with Billing Ops on 10 inbound tickets; measure reduction in manual triage steps and time-to-resolution.
Post-pilot: iterate thresholds and escalate automation opportunities to ENG for rule enforcement in Console intake form.
